newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Ruling could undo Brazil's tight pay policy.
newsitem.headline: Ruling could undo Brazil's tight pay policy.

text.p: The Brazilian government fears its policy of keeping a tight grip on payroll spending might be undone by a Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) ruling due Thursday, an official said.
The STF, Brazil's highest court, is due to rule tomorrow on a case brought by 11 civil servants who claim they are entitled to a 28.9 percent pay rise given to the armed forces in 1993.

The civil servants cite a rule that entitles workers in one sector of the public sector to pay rises awarded to state employees in other categories, the official, a spokesman at the Administration Ministry, said.
"If they won, there would be a precedent for all other federal workers," the spokesman said.
He declined to comment on reports that a ruling against the government could add about $7.0 billion to the government's payroll spending, expected to total about $42 billion in 1996.
"We hope the STF rules in favor of Brazil and not for public sector pay rises," he said.
